key_insight: ShapeR enables reliable conditional 3D object shape generation directly from casually captured, noisy image sequences by fusing sparse SLAM geometry, recognition detections, and vision-language cues to recover complete object shapes.
problem_solved: Most 3D shape generators require clean, unoccluded, well-segmented inputs; ShapeR addresses the challenge of generating complete, high-quality 3D shapes from real-world casual captures that include occlusions, sparse viewpoints, and imperfect segmentation.
method: Preprocessing pipeline: run off‑the‑shelf visual–inertial SLAM, 3D object detectors, and vision‑language models to extract per‑object sparse SLAM points, multi‑view image crops, and semantic labels.

Multimodal encoder: robustly fuse sparse geometric cues, multi‑view appearance features, and language/semantic tokens to form a conditional shape representation that tolerates missing or noisy inputs.

Conditional shape decoder: predict a complete 3D shape (implicit field / occupancy/mesh) from the fused conditional representation using training with augmentation and robustness losses to handle casual-capture artifacts.
impact: ShapeR makes it practical to build accurate 3D assets and datasets from everyday phone or handheld captures without specialized capture rigs, lowering the barrier for real-world 3D reconstruction and downstream tasks like AR, robotics, and content creation.

paper_title: ShapeR: Robust Conditional 3D Shape Generation from Casual Captures
paper_authors: Yawar Siddiqui, Duncan Frost, Samir Aroudj, Armen Avetisyan, Henry Howard-Jenkins
